$description: CORE / GLOBAL color primitives: the brand's raw color truth, shared by ALL platforms. Semantic tokens reference these; nothing downstream should hardcode a hex. Extracted from the canonical apps (Android NockerlPalettes.kt + web index.css), 2026-06.

cyan.$description: Brand cyan ramp. 500 is THE Nockerl brand color (#0CC0DF).

300.$description: Light cyan: soft fills / secondary cool accent.

500.$description: BRAND cyan. The single Nockerl accent.

700.$description: Deep cyan, tuned for white surfaces (holds AA contrast on light).

800.$description: Deep cyan (pressed / container tones on light).

900.$description: Deepest cyan, the dark end of a primary fill on light (accentPrimaryDark): a FULL ramp step below the light accentPrimary (700), so light gradients actually grade (800 was one step and read flat).

orange.$description: Brand WARM-accent ramp: the rare warm counterpart to cyan (sourced from Android's agent orange #FB923C). The ONE sanctioned warm DECORATIVE accent; used sparingly (outlines, special notices, the occasional second action). 400 reads on dark; 600 holds AA on white.

600.$description: Deep orange, tuned for white surfaces, holds AA on light (orange-600).

status.$description: Semantic STATUS hues (functional signals). Amber/red survive as genuine status ONLY. The lone sanctioned decorative warm accent is the brand `orange` ramp above (accentWarm), which is separate from statusWarning.

successDeep.$description: Deeper success for contrast on light surfaces.

warning.$description: Amber. The lone warm signal, for warnings and attention only.

categorical.$description: The tailwind-400 family used for tool families, model types, file types, task/notif/model-badge sets. A cohesive cool-leaning hue space with cyan at its center (plus orange as the warm 'agent' accent).

logo.$description: The BRAND MARK's monochrome ink system (task 2684 · law §11 CANON: the mark is MONOCHROME on every surface, and cyan lives ONLY in the lockup's product word). SURFACE-driven, not theme-driven: a host picks the ink set for the surface it sits on (ink = dark ink for light surfaces; inverse = light ink for dark surfaces). Three shades per set = the mark's layered facet ladder [base=left facet, hi=center strongest, lo=right softest]; a single flat fill is WRONG. Core layer: one identity, no new hues.

ink.$description: Dark ink, left facet (on LIGHT surfaces).

inverse.$description: Light ink, left facet (on DARK surfaces).
